chunks: Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Wahb ibn Wahb from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Volunteer (offer Nafila) prayers in the hour of unawareness, even if it be two light rak'at, for they will cause you to inherit the Abode of Generosity.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the hour of unawareness?' He replied: 'It is between the Maghrib and the Isha prayers.'

key_terms.سَاعَةُ الْغَفْلَةِ: Hour of unawareness (a specific time for voluntary prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of praying between Maghrib and Isha in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, the interval between Maghrib and Isha is viewed as a moment when the heart is less distracted by worldly affairs, making it an opportune time for spiritual reflection. Shaykh al-Saduq emphasizes that even two light rak'at offered during this 'hour of unawareness' (Sahat al-Ghafilah) serve as a means to attain the 'Abode of Generosity' (Dar al-Karamah), highlighting the transformative power of consistent, humble voluntary worship.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. Abi (rah) from Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from his father from Wahab b. Wahab from Ja’far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (a.s.) who said: “

One who offers a two rakat Nafila Salaat even if it is simple at the time of unawareness it would make him reach the door of Mercy (Paradise).” Someone asked, “O Messenger of Allah! What is this time of unawareness?” He replied, “It is between Maghrib and Isha prayers.”
